title: Data Race on Unsynchronized Shared Maps
platform_conditions: Go 1.x standard library; applies to all build targets (race detector requires -race builds)
security_mechanism: The Go runtime deliberately detects concurrent writes to a built-in map and aborts the process with 'fatal error: concurrent map writes' — not a recoverable panic — so one unsynchronized map access in a goroutine takes down the whole service. Beyond the crash, the Go memory model guarantees nothing for unsynchronized access: a goroutine that reads a flag another goroutine wrote without a happens-before edge (channel, mutex, atomic) may observe a stale or zero value, so a security check performed by one goroutine and a privileged action performed by another can interleave into a check-then-act race. Closures capturing the loop variable (pre-Go 1.22 per-loop variable semantics) additionally make every spawned goroutine observe the same final iteration value.

source_sink_clues.source: Concurrent request handlers, background workers, and callbacks sharing maps, flags, or captured loop variables without synchronization.
source_sink_clues.sink: go func() { ... m[key] = val }() on a built-in map; unsynchronized reads of shared state guarding authorization or session decisions; check-then-act sequences split across goroutines

tracking_guards: Check that shared maps are either replaced by sync.Map or confined behind a sync.Mutex/RWMutex taken on both read and write paths; check cross-goroutine security decisions use channels or sync/atomic with a happens-before edge; run -race builds in CI to observe actual races rather than reasoning about them.
not_candidate_when: The map is confined to a single goroutine and other goroutines communicate only via channels ('share memory by communicating'), every access path holds the same mutex, the variable is captured per-iteration on Go 1.22+ or via an explicit parameter, or the shared value is immutable after publication with a proper happens-before edge.
synthetic_safe_example: var mu sync.Mutex; mu.Lock(); m[key] = val; mu.Unlock()
public_references: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition') — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/362.html
CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html
